newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE'S TITAN CEMENT EYES STOCK SPLIT.
newsitem.headline: GREECE'S TITAN CEMENT EYES STOCK SPLIT.

text.p: Greece's Titan Cement will seek shareholder approval for a stock split at its annual general meeting which is scheduled for June 4, 1997, it said in its invitation to the annual assembly.
According to the agenda of the meeting, Titan Cement will capitalise reserves totalling 8.16 billion drachmas, raising stock par value from 1,620 drachmas to 2,400.
Common and preferred shares will subsequently be split into two shares with a par value of 1,200 drachmas.
Company officials said the early announcement of the proposal for the stock split was a contribution to equal information to all investors.
"The proposal for the stock split will seek approval from our shareholders at the forthcoming annual general meeting," said Spyros Xenos, public relations officer at Titan Cement.
The agenda also includes a proposal for a bond issue, but no details as to the amount of the loan were disclosed.
On a consolidated basis, Titan Cement's 1996 pre-tax earnings rose 63.2 percent to 19.2 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 10.3 percent to 108.2 billion drachmas.
Parent company earnings rose 50.2 percent to 15.7 billion drachmas. Turnover increased 15.9 percent to 74.1 billion drachmas.

Titan's common stock closed up 200 drachmas at 26,000 on Friday in volume of 7,912 shares, while preferred shares firmed 500 drachmas to 18,290 with 13,620 shares traded. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
